answer: Reputation-weighted resource lease. Each agent identity draws compute from a shared pool at the vertex of a demand curve, where price scales with how much capacity its operator already holds across all identities. Cloning forces the operator deeper into a steep canyon of rising marginal rates, since every new wallet inherits the operator's existing footprint. The velvet penalty is paid in throttled throughput: an attacker controlling N identities pays roughly N² in effective waiting time, making even modest farms uneconomic.
